newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB rates Pick "buy", sees undervalued.
newsitem.headline: CSFB rates Pick "buy", sees undervalued.

text.p: CS First Boston (CSFB) rated Hungarian meat food processor Pick Rt shares as a buy, saying the stocks are undervalued and the group has a highly desirable mix of export growth and exposure to domestic consumption.
Pick, releasing its consolidated January-September results this morning, said its profits and sales were above both last year's figure and this year's nine-month target.

Once viewed as one of the best quality and most desirable stocks on the Budapest bourse, Pick has lagged this year's exporter and construction-based market rally, CSFB analyst Spencer Jakab said in an update.

Pick shares have moved up 12 percent in 1996 against a more than 100 percent rise in dollar terms in the BUX index so far, Jakab said, adding the stocks do not deserve to trade at a discount to the market.
Jakab said Pick was an austerity-proof consumer stock whose earnings per share grew by 37.5 percent in 1995, a period when real wages dropped by around 11 percent.
If the domestic economy slid back into recession Pick would face limited direct competition, low cyclicality of earnings and a limited demand downside, Jakab said.
He also said Pick was well-positioned to expand within Hungary's food-processing sector, Jakab said.
"Pick is already more or less vertically integrated, the company's strategic position could be enhanced by acquiring companies which rely on the same distribution channels."
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Pick shares closed at 7,100 forints, up 50.
